title: QBR customer prioritization cheatgrid — fit & deployment
content:
Purpose:
Quick, scannable cheatgrid for QBR preparation and renewal prioritization that collapses ICP fit, deployment mode risk, and regional considerations into an actionable account-priority signal.

Audience:
- CS AEs and AMs preparing QBR decks
- CS managers deciding renewals outreach cadence
- Solutions/Sales Eng triage for high-risk private deployments

Overview (one line):
Map each account to a 0–100 priority score derived from: ICP fit (30 pts), deployment mode risk (25 pts), usage & health signals (25 pts), regional/compliance sensitivity (10 pts), contracts/ARR velocity (10 pts). Use threshold buckets (A/B/C) to drive QBR time allocation and renewal cadence.

TL;DR buckets (operational):
- Tier A (score >= 75): High-touch QBR + executive outreach, 2-week renewal cadence, SOW/Support review, health playbook run prior to QBR.
- Tier B (50–74): Standard QBR, CS lead + SE for deployment risk accounts, monthly enablement check-ins.
- Tier C (<50): Light-touch QBR, automated renewal emails, self-serve enablement refresh.

Scoring rubric (working draft):
1) ICP fit (0–30):
  - Strategic ICP match (enterprise AI platform, heavy inference usage) = 30
  - Core ICP match (SaaS with frequent calls, moderate tokens) = 20
  - Low fit (POC/experiment, academic) = 5–10
  - Notes: subtract 5 if customer trajectory indicates pivot away from ML workloads.

2) Deployment mode risk (0–25):
  - Private on-prem/VPC + regulated data = 25
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity) with customized routing = 18
  - Hosted (standard API) low risk = 5–10
  - Adjust: +5 if hybrid architecture with private components + hosted fallbacks (complex ops surface).

3) Usage & health signals (0–25):
  - Active daily usage with growth trend (>=15% m/m) = 25
  - Stable usage, regular calls = 15
  - Declining usage or erratic spikes, high error rates, repeated timeouts = 5
  - Include: CS health score (0–10) and infra alarms (0–15).

4) Regional / compliance sensitivity (0–10):
  - High (EU regulated, APAC regional SLAs, HIPAA) = 10
  - Moderate = 5
  - Low = 0

5) Contract / ARR velocity (0–10):
  - Near renewal within 90 days and ARR > $100k = 10
  - Renewal > 90 days or ARR < $25k = 2–4

Example calculation (sketch):
- Acme Analytics: ICP 30 + Deployment 25 + Usage 20 + Region 10 + ARR 8 = 93 => Tier A
- BetaRetail: ICP 20 + Deployment 10 + Usage 12 + Region 0 + ARR 6 = 48 => Tier C/B boundary

Action playbook by bucket (operational checklist):
- Tier A:
  - Schedule exec QBR + 60m technical deep-dive with SE
  - Prepare migration/quantization recommendations (Optimize opportunities)
  - Run pre-QBR health blitz: error logs, latency p95, cache hit rate, token cost breakdown
  - Open renewal negotiation doc + finance handover 30d out
  - If private deployment: confirm backup/failover plan and KMS status

- Tier B:
  - Standard QBR template (30m) with adoption highlights and next-steps
  - If deployment risk >= 18: add a 30m SE session to QBR agenda
  - Set adoption milestone for next 90 days; tie to incremental ARR/feature roadmap

- Tier C:
  - Automated QBR summary + product nudges (docs, new model bench reports)
  - Trigger re-engagement play if usage drops 20% quarter-over-quarter

Regional and deployment play signals (quick rules):
- EU customers with private deployments: escalate to security & compliance early; require audit checklist completed before QBR.
- APAC customers on hosted API: check regional latency counters; propose regional routing if p95 > 400ms.
- On-prem customers with low usage: assess cost-to-serve and propose dedicated vs. hosted cost analysis.

QBR prep checklist (to paste into deck):
- Snapshot: ARR, contract end, seat counts, active endpoints, tokens/day
- Top 3 wins last period, top 3 blockers, proposed mitigations
- Deployment risks & mitigations (network, KMS, patching cadence)
- Cost levers used: batching, quantization, caching — potential savings estimate
- Ask list: executive sponsor availability, renewal timeline, willingness to pilot dedicated/Private

Data sources and signals (where to pull from):
- Product telemetry: tokens/day, p95 latency, errors/timeframe (SRE/observability)
- Console: model versions in use, KV cache hit rates, routing policies
- Billing: net ARR, invoicing, committed vs. overage trends
- Support: open cases, escalations in last 90d
- Account/CS notes: exec relationships, roadmap alignment

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Finalize weights: does deployment risk deserve 25 pts or 30? experiment with 50-account cohort.
- Can we automate scoring in Console export? (see linked GH PR)
- Create looker dashboard: regional risk heatmap + 90-day renewal overlay (owner: Liam)
- Validate thresholds for Tier A in low-ARR enterprise accounts (edge cases).

Quick templates to paste into QBR slide notes:
- Executive summary line: "This QBR recommends Tier A engagement due to private deployment risk, 92% utilization growth, and a renewal in 60 days — propose exec sync and a pre-renewal technical audit."
- Technical ask: "Request 2-hour maintenance window next month to validate KV cache and failover behavior for private deployment."

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally compact. Ops team wants something pasteable into QBR decks.
- Reach out to Solutions Eng to add a one-pager for private-deployment preflight checklist.
- Next iteration: add a 'likelihood to expand' signal from sales CRM (lead score).
